item.text:
**3B.6 Research Note**

Bottom line: Lula’s 2024 record is more consistent with **bounded legal controls and policing reforms** than with state terror or a generalized fear climate. The main weakness is that Brazil’s underlying police-violence and prison-abuse problems clearly persisted, so the reforms did not yet translate into fully safe conditions.

- [Portaria MJSP nº 648, de 28 de maio de 2024](http://dspace.mj.gov.br/handle/1/12967) — Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública — 2024-05-28  
  - Claim-level summary: the ministry created national body-camera guidelines for public security agencies, emphasizing recording, transparency, evidence preservation, and tighter control of police conduct. This is the clearest 2024 example of reducing fear through oversight rather than intimidation.  
  - Question IDs: 3B.6, 3B.5, 3B.4, 3B.1

- [MJSP lança diagnóstico sobre o uso de câmeras corporais pelos agentes de segurança pública](https://www.gov.br/mj/pt-br/assuntos/noticias/mjsp-lanca-diagnostico-sobre-o-uso-de-cameras-corporais-pelos-agentes-de-seguranca-publica) — Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública — 2024-07-31  
  - Claim-level summary: the ministry said body cameras are associated with more reporting and lower police lethality. That supports a strategy of lowering domestic insecurity without substituting it with state terror.  
  - Question IDs: 3B.6, 3B.5, 3B.4, 3B.1

- [Decreto nº 12.341, de 23 de dezembro de 2024](https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2023-2026/2024/decreto/d12341.htm) — Presidência da República / Planalto — 2024-12-23  
  - Claim-level summary: Lula regulated police use of force and less-lethal tools, explicitly framing the reform around legality, precaution, necessity, due process, and non-discrimination. This is evidence for lawful restraint rather than a fear-based security posture.  
  - Question IDs: 3B.6, 3B.5, 3B.4, 3B.1

- [Decreto nº 12.167, de 6 de setembro de 2024](https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2023-2026/2024/decreto/d12167.htm) — Presidência da República / Planalto — 2024-09-06  
  - Claim-level summary: the Armed Forces were authorized for election security only in specified localities and for defined periods, under electoral-court coordination. That is a bounded, lawful use of security powers rather than open-ended coercion.  
  - Question IDs: 3B.6, 3B.5

- [GLO em portos e aeroportos é prorrogada pelo presidente Lula por 30 dias](https://www.gov.br/portos-e-aeroportos/pt-br/assuntos/noticias/2024/05/glo-em-portos-e-aeroportos-e-prorrogada-pelo-presidente-lula-por-30-dias) — Ministério de Portos e Aeroportos — 2024-05-06  
  - Claim-level summary: Lula extended a GLO deployment in coordination with civilian authorities; the page describes inspections, seizures, and coordinated security. This is evidence of narrow administrative control, not broad political fear-mongering.  
  - Question IDs: 3B.6, 3B.5

- [Decreto nº 12.006, de 24 de abril de 2024](https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2023-2026/2024/decreto/d12006.htm) — Presidência da República / Planalto — 2024-04-24  
  - Claim-level summary: school-violence reporting was integrated into national security information channels and an emergency number, which is a targeted administrative response to domestic insecurity rather than generalized surveillance.  
  - Question IDs: 3B.6, 3B.5

- [Brazil: Comply with Rulings on Police Violence](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/15/brazil-comply-rulings-police-violence) — Human Rights Watch — 2024-03-15  
  - Claim-level summary: HRW said Brazil still had not fully implemented independent-investigation requirements for police killings and that lethal raids and unlawful force continued. This is strong counterevidence that domestic fear and insecurity were still being reproduced by abusive policing.  
  - Question IDs: 3B.6, 3B.5, 3B.4, 3B.1

- [World Report 2025: Brazil](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2025/country-chapters/brazil) — Human Rights Watch — 2025-01-01, covering 2024 events  
  - Claim-level summary: HRW reported continued police killings in 2024 and prison conditions marked by overcrowding and ill-treatment/torture. That is the strongest evidence that reforms had not yet eliminated abuse-driven fear.  
  - Question IDs: 3B.6, 3B.5, 3B.4, 3B.1

Search gap: I did not find reliable 2024 evidence that Lula used emergency powers or security laws to create a broader political fear climate. I also did not find strong direct outcome evidence that public fear or insecurity fell nationwide; what exists is mainly policy and oversight evidence, plus clear counterevidence that police and prison abuse remained serious.
